title: Antibacterial, Optical, Structural, and AC Conductivity Characteristics of Lithium-Doped Barium Zinc Borate Glasses for Multiple Applications
abstract:
<jats:p>An Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O-incorporated bioactive glass system of chemical composition xLi<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O-10BaO-10ZnO-(80-x)B<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>3</jats:sub> with x = 0–20 mol% was synthesized by melt-quench route. Non-crystalline behaviour was confirmed with X-ray diffraction spectra. The antibacterial zone of inhibitions increased with Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O incorporation. Experimental densities increased with Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O molar content and molar volume decreased. UV-Optical absorption spectra confirmed a cut-off wave length (<jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>c</jats:sub>) increasing trend by NBOs. Indirect band gap decreased, direct band gap decreased, and Urbach energy increased with Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O addition. The refractive index of the glass system also increased. Fourier transform infrared and Raman spectroscopy studies confirmed the structural variations and existence of metal-oxides in the glass matrix. The AC conductivity increased with frequency, temperature, and also Li<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O content by almost three orders of magnitude. The findings of higher order conductivity (10<jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>Ω<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>cm<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>), improvement in the zone of inhibitions upto 15 mm against <jats:italic>E. coli</jats:italic>., and 14 mm against Salmonella; higher value of refractive index (n > 2) confirms the multiple applications of these glasses.</jats:p>
journal: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology
